teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). All three are official teaching languages of the programme and admission is language-position based, not language-specific. English is genuinely used (e.g. the mathematics preparatory course is held in English; 'Refreshing English' 2 CP in year 1 and 'Scientific Writing in English' 6 CP in year 2 are compulsory), but Italian and German carry equal official weight, and the two compulsory 'Foreign Language 1 / Foreign Language 2' course pairs (3+3 CP in year 1, 3+3 CP in year 2) are explicitly German/Italian-as-a-foreign-language specialised language courses. Students who graduated in a language other than the three official teaching languages must nominate the two languages in which they will sit the language exams. unibz does not publish a percentage split of teaching hours per language for this programme. [uncertain]
campus: Bozen-Bolzano (main campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano). Faculty of Economics and Management. Single campus — no NOI Techpark, Brixen, Bruneck or external-site component.
degree_class: L-18 (Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale / Economics and Business Administration). Confirmed on the 2026/27 official brochure: 'Bachelor class: L-18'. The admission PDF also references L-18 when explaining the double-enrolment rule.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with competitive ranking. No entrance examination, no TOLC, no SAT, no interview and no portfolio. Selection is a document- and grade-based dossier evaluation performed by the Admission Committee on the basis of self-declared secondary-school grades plus language-certificate bonus points. Applications are submitted through the unibz Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/). Separate quotas and procedures apply to (1) EU citizens and those given parity of treatment and (2) non-EU citizens living abroad. Selection criteria approved by Faculty of Economics Faculty Council Resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025.
academic_requirements: Secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system, OR an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if it was obtained after 12 years of education AND at least the last two years were attended within that foreign school system (unibz gives the Irish Leaving Certificate as the counter-example: attending only one year and obtaining the certificate is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain qualifications — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly — and applicants in those categories are told to contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service) before applying. No specific subject prerequisites, no minimum GPA gate other than the ranking threshold, and no prior ECTS/SSD requirement (this is a bachelor programme, so the SSD-credit logic that applies to unibz master admissions is not relevant here). Candidates who have not yet graduated may apply and upload the diploma at enrolment. Under national rules, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of two programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same degree class (e.g. not L-18 with another L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of course content. Language requirements (see language section) are a hard admission gate — failing them means exclusion from the procedure before any ranking.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and language requirements are a hard exclusion gate — failing them means exclusion from the admission procedure before ranking, not a lower score. Requirements are defined by POSITION (1st/2nd/3rd language), not by which language: your first language is the one you are strongest in, your third is the one you are weakest in or an absolute beginner in. Entry: B2 in the 1st language, B2 in the 2nd language, no level required in the 3rd. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and only recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. A B1 in the third language is the minimum to sit curricular exams in that language, and if the first semester is taught only in English while English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January to take all first-semester exams. Free Language Centre courses target B1 in the third language by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2; three-week intensive courses run in September (2026/27: 01–18/09/2026, Mon–Fri, 6 h/day) and A1 beginner courses are now offered ONLY in that September window, so absolute beginners must start there. Extensive courses (4 h/week) run during semesters, intensive courses (6 h/day) between semesters. Higher-than-required levels earn up to 3 ranking bonus points.
application_deadline_eu: Two sessions were open for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment in 2026/27; the third (Additional) session was NOT offered for this programme. (1) EARLY BIRD — application 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08, by noon local time (28/05 - 08/07/2026). Applicants excluded in the first session may re-apply in the second, and EU applicants may apply to more than one study programme. (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION — window 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04 university-wide, but the additional-session page lists Bachelor in Economics and Management as 'Application NOT offered', so this route did not exist for this programme in 2026/27. NOTE: as of the verification date (2026-08-29) the entire 2026/27 cycle is closed; 2027/28 dates are not yet published.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (Early Bird, unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). Non-EU citizens living outside Italy have no Late Application and no Additional Session — 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies. Downstream 2026/27 dates were the same as Early Bird: ranking by 2026-05-27, first instalment by 2026-06-05 (noon), enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 (noon). Universitaly pre-enrolment is mandatory after paying the first instalment, and admission on the ranking list is granted 'with reservation' until the Italian consulate confirms directly to unibz.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION (uploaded in the unibz Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): (1) a valid ID card or passport, front and back — an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document means exclusion from the admission procedure; (2) the completed online application form, including self-declaration of the grades for the four subject areas plus two extra subjects for each of the two relevant high-school years (German secondary schools: the 'Jahreszeugnis' grades, or the average of the two 'Halbjahreszeugnisse' with decimal place if unavailable); (3) a copy of the relevant school report cards where a self-declared year was completed abroad; (4) official translation of the school report cards into Italian, German or English where needed; (5) optionally, language certificates for the bonus-point calculation and for proving entry levels; (6) the diploma of the qualification if already obtained (otherwise at enrolment). Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Once sent, the application cannot be modified, and forms that are filled in but not correctly submitted are disregarded. AT ENROLMENT, for a foreign secondary-school qualification: the diploma; an official Italian translation (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); and the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. NOTE: the structured 'study career' Excel template that unibz requires for master's applications is NOT part of this bachelor procedure. Transfer students from another Italian university must additionally submit a copy of the transfer application filed at their previous university to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. unibz may request further documents in case of doubt and can exclude a student by Rector's decree even after enrolment if the admission qualification is not valid.
entry_exam_or_test: NO admission entrance exam of any kind — unibz does not use its own subject test, TOLC-I, TOLC-E, CENT-S, SAT or GMAT/GRE for this programme. Admission is purely dossier/ranking based.

Language proficiency exams (optional route, only if you cannot prove your levels by diploma or recognised certificate): organised online by the unibz Language Centre. 2026/27 Early Bird sittings 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 + 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); Late Application sittings 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). Registration is done inside the application portal under 'enrol for language exams'. Note: only B2-level exams can be booked.

Compulsory mathematics test — AFTER admission, not for admission. The faculty runs a mathematics preparatory course in English before the first semester (2026/27: 21–25/09/2026) and every new student must sit a compulsory test at the end of it. A negative result or non-participation triggers OFA (see ofa_rules). Test topics are published at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Economics/OFA-Topics26.pdf (English only).
Third-language placement test — after admission, for students who cannot certify their third language; determines the assigned language-learning path.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/economics-management/fees — EUR 1,200 per year for students within the normal programme length, split into two instalments of EUR 600. The 1st instalment includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and, in the admission procedure, is the payment that secures the admitted place (2026/27 admission deadlines: 05/06/2026 Early Bird, 06/08/2026 Late). Once enrolled, the faculty fee calendar is 1st instalment by 13/10/2026 and 2nd instalment by 31/03/2027 (the admission PDF states more generally 'by March of the following year'). Late payment of the second instalment incurs a EUR 30 fine and blocks exam registration and mySNS access; unpaid fees also block transfer to other universities or programmes. Students beyond the normal programme length (fuori corso) pay EUR 1,500 (EUR 900 + EUR 600). No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Full exemption (paying only the EUR 16 stamp) for students with a disability recognised under art. 3 para. 1 of Law 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or more — the health-authority certificate must be handed in at the start of the academic year — and for foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Holders of a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees, usually in March–April.
official_call_url: No separate call/manifesto document is published in English for this programme — the admission-information PDF functions as the official call. The underlying legal act is Faculty of Economics Faculty Council Resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025, which approved the 2026/27 selection criteria; it is cited in the ranking-list PDFs but is not published as a standalone downloadable file on unibz.it. Related official pages: application portal https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ and additional-application-session page https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/additional-application-session [uncertain]

Degree class and profile (2026/27 brochure, 'At a glance'): 'Bachelor class: L-18; ECTS credits: 180; Duration of the course: 3 years; Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual); Places available: 150 EU + 5 non-EU; Campus: Bozen-Bolzano; Tuition fees: ca. uncertainty_notes: 1) CYCLE STATUS — all data here is the 2026/27 cycle, which is already CLOSED as of the verification date (2026-08-29): both application windows have passed, both ranking lists are published and signed, and the additional session did not include this programme. The 2027/28 call, quotas and dates are not yet published; expect the same structure (Early Bird ~early March to late April, Late ~late May to early July) but treat every specific date above as historical rather than actionable. 2) The two official PDFs both carry 'Latest update: 24.08.2026' and are explicitly marked 'Subject to change'. 3) TEACHING-LANGUAGE WEIGHTING is not published — unibz states the programme is trilingual and the study plan shows which language courses are compulsory, but no percentage split of teaching hours by language is given anywhere, and the course-level language assignment is not stated on the public study plan page. The teaching_language field is therefore marked uncertain on the weighting only; the trilingual classification itself is certain. 4) FIRST INTAKE YEAR is not published; the 'not a new programme' assessment rests on ranking lists existing at least back to 2017. 5) OFFICIAL CALL — there is no standalone English call/manifesto PDF; Faculty Council Resolution 142/15.09.2025 is cited in the ranking lists but not downloadable, so official_call_url is a best-effort answer. 6) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS (EUR 1,680–6,960) come from the unibz Study Guide rather than the current provincial call and may be a prior-year figure. 7) TURKEY'S CREDENTIAL TIER (ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification) is inferred from Turkey's Lisbon Convention membership; unibz publishes the rule by tier, not by country, so Turkish applicants should confirm with apply@unibz.it. 8) The faculty fee-calendar dates (13/10/2026 and 31/03/2027) come from guide.unibz.it and are slightly more specific than the admission PDF's 'by March of the following year' — no contradiction, different granularity. 9) The ranking-list PDFs are published only in Italian and German; the English admission PDF does not report cut-off scores, so all cut-off figures were read from the bilingual IT/DE ranking documents. 10) An English-only applicant is treated here as effectively excluded — this is an interpretation of the B2/B2 position rule, but it is corroborated by the large exclusion blocks 'for not meeting the language requirements' in both 2026/27 ranking lists (8 non-EU and dozens of EU applicants).
